name: Morehead Star Theater
campus: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
address: 250 East Franklin Street, Chapel Hill, NC 27599
coordinate_source: Worldwide Planetariums Database sheet for this theater. Altitude printed there as 144 m; an earlier sheet of the same database printed 145 m.

dome.height_note: Floor to apex, as published by Morehead for the fulldome theater. A 68 ft diameter hemisphere would rise 34 ft, so the extra height is the cove under the spring line, not a deeper sphere.

projectors.notes: Bought in Sweden. Stockholm exhibition instrument of 1930, stored in Stockholm, then Göteborg, installed for the 10 May 1949 opening. Planetarium-database history calls a 1959 servicing an upgrade toward Model III. RocketSTEM describes that work as a correction of the 42 brightest stars. Mercury and Gemini training used this machine.
One of nine Model VI instruments. Clearer field, eclipse devices, redesigned console. Neil Armstrong was the first astronaut to train on it. Decommissioned April 2011; removed by August 2011.
GlaxoSmithKline Fulldome Theater. Sky-Skan Definiti, later a 4K edge-blended pair (north half and south half). The training-era view is a reconstruction. The Zeiss is not in the pit.

projection.geometry: Hemisphere centered on the instrument, near the center of the dome sphere. Horizon is a diaphragm of shutters on the star-sphere lenses, not a second catalog.
projection.why_6_5: Matches the published Zeiss plate limit of about 8,900 stars. A modern digital catalog goes much fainter and would not be the training sky.
projection.plate_stand_in: Yale Bright Star Catalog or Hipparcos, stars brighter than magnitude 6.5. The perforated plates themselves are not reproduced in this folder.
projection.training_view_is_not_the_local_horizon: Instructors drove daily motion and the latitude axis so stars sat where a spacecraft window would see them. Chapel Hill's latitude is the public-show default, not the astronaut view.
